- **Minnesota Twins (home) moneyline (+107, BetRivers)** -- [44faa9639a3a54e8] event=33fe59d6a76323b4bbbed9cc6cf368e9 selection_id=9e8d61f45a38abf0 edge_bps=None p_model_provenance=none grade=A
  - because: Backing the home side of h2h because 1 pre-registered signal fired: (1) starter_velocity_gap -- how far the opposing starter's fastball sits above league pace (each side's number describes the matchup that side's own lineup faces): away 3.28 mph, home 0.37 mph (this game's own values rest on: away over 222 measured fastballs; home over 315 measured fastballs); a gap of 2.91 mph, clearing the threshold of 1.96 mph (rung 1 of 3, the 50th percentile of that gap over the ladder's derivation sample, 3,149 games with both sides measured, 2023-24). This mechanism's direction was frozen before any search ran at -1 (the side holding more of it is the side the mechanism harms), so the signal points to the home side. Pre-registered reason it should matter: a starter whose fastball sits above league pace is holding stuff the season line has not caught up to, so the lineup facing the harder thrower is the disadvantaged side; velocity leads results and the market prices results. This is a signal count, not a forecast: the genome publishes no calibrated probability, so p_model is null and edge_bps is null by construction. Nothing here says the market's price is mistaken, and no claim of value is attached to it -- no such claim has been earned (docs/PREREG_CALIBRATED_PROBABILITY.md). (Strategy: evolab genome 44faa9639a3a54e8.)

- **Washington Nationals (home) moneyline (-149, LowVig.ag)** -- [2bff17328ce70639] event=4e9f6bd2e2e14a12f13b59aec5f1cc9b selection_id=9e8d61f45a38abf0 edge_bps=None p_model_provenance=none grade=A
  - because: Backing the home side of h2h because 3 pre-registered signals fired: (1) lineup_platoon_share -- the share of the posted lineup holding the platoon advantage over the starter it faces (each side's number describes the matchup that side's own lineup faces): away 37.5%, home 66.7% (this game's own values rest on: away over 9 lineup slots; home over 9 lineup slots); a gap of 29.2 percentage points, clearing the threshold of 22.2 percentage points (rung 1 of 3, the 50th percentile of that gap over the ladder's derivation sample, 4,856 games with both sides measured, 2023-24). This mechanism's direction was frozen before any search ran at +1 (the side holding more of it is the side the mechanism favours), so the signal points to the home side. Pre-registered reason it should matter: the classic exploitation: a lineup posted one-handed against a starter it holds the platoon advantage over gets more of its plate appearances in the favourable split than the club-level season line the market prices ever reflects. (2) primary_pitch_share -- the share of pitches the opposing starter throws with his single most-used offering (each side's number describes the matchup that side's own lineup faces): away 31.9%, home 42.0% (this game's own values rest on: away over 3,396 pitches; home over 9,672 pitches); a gap of 10.1 percentage points, clearing the threshold of 9.7 percentage points (rung 1 of 3, the 50th percentile of that gap over the ladder's derivation sample, 4,061 games with both sides measured, 2023-24). This mechanism's direction was frozen before any search ran at +1 (the side holding more of it is the side the mechanism favours), so the signal points to the home side. Pre-registered reason it should matter: concentration in one pitch is predictability: the more of a starter's arsenal is a single offering, the more of the lineup's preparation transfers, and pitch-level lean is not a term in any club-level price. (3) starter_groundball_share -- the opposing starter's career ground-ball share (each side's number describes the matchup that side's own lineup faces): away 51.9%, home 40.8% (this game's own values rest on: away over 576 batted balls; home over 1,618 batted balls); a gap of 11.1 percentage points, clearing the threshold of 6.5 percentage points (rung 1 of 3, the 50th percentile of that gap over the ladder's derivation sample, 3,516 games with both sides measured, 2023-24). This mechanism's direction was frozen before any search ran at -1 (the side holding more of it is the side the mechanism harms), so the signal points to the home side. Pre-registered reason it should matter: a career ground-ball starter takes the air out of an offence that lives on balls in the air, so the lineup facing the higher ground-ball share is the disadvantaged side and club-level pricing averages the collision out. This is a signal count, not a forecast: the genome publishes no calibrated probability, so p_model is null and edge_bps is null by construction. Nothing here says the market's price is mistaken, and no claim of value is attached to it -- no such claim has been earned (docs/PREREG_CALIBRATED_PROBABILITY.md). (Strategy: evolab genome 2bff17328ce70639.)

  - because: Backing the away side of h2h_1st_5_innings because 1 pre-registered signal fired: (1) lineup_platoon_share -- the share of the posted lineup holding the platoon advantage over the starter it faces (each side's number describes the matchup that side's own lineup faces): away 57.1%, home 33.3% (this game's own values rest on: away over 9 lineup slots; home over 9 lineup slots); a gap of 23.8 percentage points, clearing the threshold of 22.2 percentage points (rung 1 of 3, the 50th percentile of that gap over the ladder's derivation sample, 4,856 games with both sides measured, 2023-24). This is a signal count, not a forecast: the genome publishes no calibrated probability, so p_model is null and edge_bps is null by construction. Nothing here says the market's price is mistaken, and no claim of value is attached to it -- no such claim has been earned (docs/PREREG_CALIBRATED_PROBABILITY.md).
